events.quote: To ask for something nicely, use "Can I have + thing, please?" or "I would like + thing, please."

next_task.correct: Can I have a tea, please?

events.quote: Rule: some verbs do not take -ed; they change to a new word, like go to went.
Right: She saw a bird yesterday. Wrong: She seed a bird yesterday.
Rule: say am, is or are, then "going to", then the action word.
Right: He is going to swim this weekend. Wrong: He going to swim this weekend.

next_task.correct: I am going to study tonight.

events.quote: For regular verbs, add -ed to make the past simple
The rule: some verbs change instead of taking -ed, like go to went, buy to bought, see to saw.
Right: She saw a cat. Wrong: She seed a cat.
After he, she or it, we add -s to the verb
After -sh, -ch, -s, -x or -o, we add -es: watch -> watches. Consonant + y becomes -ies
Rule: for a finished action, add -ed to most verbs.
Right: They opened the window yesterday. Wrong: They open the window yesterday.
The rule: after can, use the plain verb, with no -s.
Right: My friend can sing. Wrong: My friend can sings.
For plans we use am/is/are + going to + verb.

next_task.correct: I am going to study tonight.

events.quote: We use am/is/are + verb-ing for things happening now.
We use am/is/are + verb-ing for things happening now.
We use "the" when we talk about something again. First time: "a". Second time: "the".
Rule: after he, she, it or one person's name, add -s or -es to the action word.
Right: Lina cooks every evening. Wrong: Lina cook every evening.
The rule: use am with I, is with he, she or it, and are with you, we or they.
Rule: for a finished action in the past, add -ed to most verbs.
Right: My friend called me on Sunday. Wrong: My friend call me on Sunday.
Some verbs do not take -ed in the past. They have a special form.
We say 'I went to the market yesterday', not 'I goed'.
Rule: use at before a clock time.
Right: We have dinner at 7 o'clock. Wrong: We have dinner in 7 o'clock.
start every sentence with a capital letter, always write the word I as a capital, and finish with a full stop.
Remember: after did, the verb stays in the base form (go, not went).
To ask about the past, use: (question word) + did + person + base verb.
